raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

`docs/design/arch_overview.md` documents the V1 process architecture
(API server, engine core, GPU workers, DP coordinator) but has no
explanation of how the scheduler works internally. New contributors
reading this doc have no entry point into understanding scheduling,
preemption, or async scheduling behaviour.

Adds a `## Scheduler` section covering the token-budget model, FCFS/Priority policies, recompute-based preemption, and async scheduling at a conceptual level (no private field names, so it shouldn't drift with refactors).

Relates to Q1 2026 Docs SIG goal: educational material for architecture
and internals.

## Test Plan

Documentation-only change. No code is modified.

Verified that the rendered Markdown is structurally correct and that
all internal hyperlinks to source files resolve on main.

## Test Result

N/A — documentation only.

Part of #32455

nodes.body: Rebased and fixed both points. Replaced `discard_latest_async_tokens` with the current `num_stale_output_tokens`/`drop_stale_output` fields, and corrected the preemption description: every `_preempt_request` call marks in-flight output stale and still delivers it by default, only `drop_stale_output=True` (used by `reset_prefix_cache`) discards it.

✅ Triggered [Buildkite CI #98345](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98345) for commit `6abdd830efeb`.

ℹ️ This PR is 1650 commits behind upstream `main`. Merged upstream `main` into this branch as `6abdd830efeb` before starting CI. Pull the branch before pushing more changes.

## Code Review

This pull request adds a comprehensive 'Scheduler' section to the architecture overview documentation, explaining the V1 scheduler's token-budget-based logic, scheduling policies, and preemption behavior. A review comment points out a discrepancy between the documented async scheduling preemption logic and the actual implementation, which could lead to duplicate output tokens if not addressed.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The documentation states that AsyncScheduler resets num_output_placeholders to 0 and sets discard_latest_async_tokens = True whenever a request is preempted. However, the current implementation in vllm/v1/core/sched/async_scheduler.py does not override _preempt_request, and the base Scheduler._preempt_request (lines 949-970 in scheduler.py) does not perform these actions. These fields are currently only updated during a prefix cache reset (lines 1876-1880 in scheduler.py). This discrepancy could lead to the 'spurious duplicate output token' issue the documentation claims to prevent if a request is preempted due to cache pressure. Please either update the implementation to include these actions in the general preemption path or clarify the documentation to reflect the current behavior.

+## Scheduler
+
+The scheduler runs inside the **Engine Core Process** and is responsible for
+deciding which requests execute each step. Its source is in
+[vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py](../../vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py).
+
+The V1 scheduler is **token-budget-based**: at each step it holds a fixed
+`max_num_scheduled_tokens` budget and fills it greedily across both running and
+waiting requests. There is no separate "prefill phase" or "decode phase" —
+each request has a `num_computed_tokens` counter that advances toward
+`num_tokens_with_spec`. This unified view handles chunked prefills, prefix
+caching, and speculative decoding within a single scheduling loop.
+
+### Scheduling Policies
+
+Two policies are supported via `--scheduling-policy`:
+
+-   **FCFS** (default): requests are scheduled first-come, first-served. When
+    the KV cache is exhausted, the last-admitted running request is preempted.
+-   **Priority**: requests carry an integer `priority` field. When the KV cache
+    is exhausted, the running request with the lowest priority (highest
+    `priority` value, then latest arrival time) is preempted.
+
+### Preemption
+
+When the KV cache is exhausted and a request cannot be allocated new blocks,
+the scheduler **preempts** a lower-priority running request:
+
+1.  Its KV cache blocks are freed immediately.
+2.  `num_computed_tokens` is reset to `0` — the request must recompute from
+    scratch when re-admitted.
+3.  The request is prepended to the front of the waiting queue with
+    `PREEMPTED` status, so it is re-admitted before any new requests.
+
+!!! note
+    vLLM V1 does not swap KV cache to CPU memory. Preempted requests always
+    recompute. Prefix caching makes this inexpensive for requests that share
+    a common prompt prefix.
+
+### Async Scheduling
+
+`AsyncScheduler`
+([vllm/v1/core/sched/async_scheduler.py](../../vllm/v1/core/sched/async_scheduler.py))
+is a thin subclass of `Scheduler` that overlaps CPU scheduling with GPU
+execution: while the GPU executes step *N*, the CPU speculatively schedules
+step *N+1*.
+
+Each scheduled decode step adds an **output placeholder**
+(`num_output_placeholders`) to the request — a token slot for a result the
+GPU is producing but has not yet returned. When a request is preempted while
+async scheduling is active, `AsyncScheduler` additionally:
+
+-   Resets `num_output_placeholders` to `0`.
+-   Sets `discard_latest_async_tokens = True` on the request.

nodes.body: ## Pull request overview Adds a new **Scheduler** section to the V1 architecture overview to give contributors an entry point into how V1 scheduling, preemption, and async scheduling work. **Changes:** - Document the token-budget-based scheduling model (and lack of strict prefill/decode phase separation). - Describe FCFS vs Priority scheduling and their eviction behavior under KV pressure. - Explain preemption mechanics and async scheduling concepts (output placeholders, token discard behavior). --- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. Learn how to get started.

`num_computed_tokens` is reset to 0 on preemption, but when the request is re-admitted the scheduler may immediately restore a non-zero computed-token count via prefix caching (and/or externally matched KV tokens via the KVConnector). Describing this as “recompute from scratch” is inaccurate; consider rephrasing to “recompute missing tokens (no CPU swap), potentially skipping cached prefixes.”
```suggestion
2.  `num_computed_tokens` is reset to `0`. When the request is re-admitted, it
    recomputes only the missing tokens (no KV swap to CPU), and the scheduler
    may immediately restore progress via prefix caching or externally matched
    KV tokens.
3.  The request is prepended to the front of the waiting queue with
    `PREEMPTED` status, so it is re-admitted before any new requests.

!!! note
    vLLM V1 does not swap KV cache to CPU memory. Preempted requests
    recompute missing tokens but may skip cached prefixes. Prefix caching
    makes this inexpensive for requests that share a common prompt prefix.
```

nodes.body: `AsyncScheduler` does not override `_preempt_request`, and regular KV-exhaustion preemption does not reset `num_output_placeholders` or set `discard_latest_async_tokens`. Those fields are set during forced preemption in `Scheduler.reset_prefix_cache(reset_running_requests=True)`. Consider updating this paragraph to reference the reset-prefix-cache path (or otherwise qualify when these fields are modified).

nodes.body:
In async scheduling, each scheduled non-prefill step increments `num_output_placeholders` by `1 + num_spec_tokens_scheduled` (to account for draft/spec tokens), not strictly by 1. Wording like “adds one or more output placeholders” (or mentioning the speculative-decoding case) would better match the implementation.
```suggestion
Each scheduled decode step adds one or more **output placeholders**
(`num_output_placeholders`) to the request — one for the main token plus any
speculative (draft/spec) tokens the GPU is producing but has not yet
returned. When a request is preempted while async scheduling is active,
`AsyncScheduler` additionally:
```

nodes.body:
The statement that a preempted request is “prepended to the front of the waiting queue … so it is re-admitted before any new requests” only holds for FCFS. Under the Priority policy, `prepend_request` re-inserts into a heap ordered by (priority, arrival_time), so a preempted request can be scheduled after newly arrived higher-priority requests.
```suggestion
3.  The request is re-queued with `PREEMPTED` status:
    - Under **FCFS**, it is prepended to the front of the waiting queue, so it
      is re-admitted before any later-arriving requests.
    - Under **Priority**, it is reinserted into the priority queue ordered by
      `(priority, arrival_time)`, so newly arrived higher-priority requests
      may still be scheduled first.
```

+    may immediately restore progress via prefix caching or externally matched
+    KV tokens.

+      is re-admitted before any later-arriving requests.

+      `(priority, arrival_time)`, so newly arrived higher-priority requests
+      may still be scheduled first.

+    vLLM V1 does not swap KV cache to CPU memory. Preempted requests
+    recompute missing tokens but may skip cached prefixes. Prefix caching
+    makes this inexpensive for requests that share a common prompt prefix.

+step *N+1*.

detail.body:
## Purpose

`docs/design/arch_overview.md` documents the V1 process architecture
(API server, engine core, GPU workers, DP coordinator) but has no
explanation of how the scheduler works internally. New contributors
reading this doc have no entry point into understanding scheduling,
preemption, or async scheduling behaviour.

Adds a `## Scheduler` section covering the token-budget model, FCFS/Priority policies, recompute-based preemption, and async scheduling at a conceptual level (no private field names, so it shouldn't drift with refactors).

Relates to Q1 2026 Docs SIG goal: educational material for architecture
and internals.

## Test Plan

Documentation-only change. No code is modified.

Verified that the rendered Markdown is structurally correct and that
all internal hyperlinks to source files resolve on main.

## Test Result

N/A — documentation only.

Part of #32455

 For CPU resource sizing recommendations, see
 [CPU Resources for GPU Deployments](../configuration/optimization.md#cpu-resources-for-gpu-deployments).
 
+## Scheduler
+
+The scheduler runs inside the **Engine Core Process** and decides which
+requests execute each step. The code can be found in
+[vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py](../../vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py).
+
+The scheduler is **token-budget-based**: each step, it fills a budget of
+`max_num_batched_tokens` across both running and waiting requests. There are no
+separate prefill and decode phases. Each request tracks how many of its tokens
+have been computed, and the scheduler assigns it tokens to close the gap. This
+single loop handles chunked prefill, prefix caching and speculative decoding.
+
+### Scheduling Policies
+
+Two policies are supported via `--scheduling-policy`:
+
+- **FCFS** (default): requests are scheduled first-come, first-served. When
+    the KV cache is exhausted, the last-admitted running request is preempted.
+- **Priority**: requests carry an integer `priority` field. When the KV cache
+    is exhausted, the running request with the lowest priority (highest
+    `priority` value, then latest arrival time) is preempted.
+
+### Preemption
+
+When a request cannot be allocated new KV cache blocks, the scheduler
+**preempts** running requests, chosen by the scheduling policy, until enough
+blocks are free:
+
+1. The preempted request's KV cache blocks are freed.
+2. Its progress is reset and it returns to the waiting queue. Under FCFS it
+    goes to the front of the queue; under Priority it is reinserted by
+    `(priority, arrival_time)`.
+3. When re-admitted, it is recomputed rather than swapped back from CPU
+    memory. Prefix caching or a KV connector can restore part of its progress
+    immediately.
+
+For how to reduce preemption, see
+[Preemption](../configuration/optimization.md#preemption).
+
+### Async Scheduling
+
+With async scheduling,
+[vllm/v1/core/sched/async_scheduler.py](../../vllm/v1/core/sched/async_scheduler.py)
+overlaps CPU scheduling with GPU execution: while the GPU executes step *N*,
+the CPU schedules step *N+1*, using placeholders for the tokens that step *N*
+will produce.
+
+If a request is preempted while it still has output in flight, that output is
+normally still delivered when it arrives. It is dropped instead when delivering
+it would be invalid, for example when `reset_prefix_cache` preempts and resumes
+requests within the same step.
+

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The documentation states that AsyncScheduler resets num_output_placeholders to 0 and sets discard_latest_async_tokens = True whenever a request is preempted. However, the current implementation in vllm/v1/core/sched/async_scheduler.py does not override _preempt_request, and the base Scheduler._preempt_request (lines 949-970 in scheduler.py) does not perform these actions. These fields are currently only updated during a prefix cache reset (lines 1876-1880 in scheduler.py). This discrepancy could lead to the 'spurious duplicate output token' issue the documentation claims to prevent if a request is preempted due to cache pressure. Please either update the implementation to include these actions in the general preemption path or clarify the documentation to reflect the current behavior.

+    is exhausted, the running request with the lowest priority (highest
+    `priority` value, then latest arrival time) is preempted.

+the scheduler **preempts** a lower-priority running request:

+    recomputes only the missing tokens (no KV swap to CPU), and the scheduler
+    may immediately restore progress via prefix caching or externally matched
+    KV tokens.

+([vllm/v1/core/sched/async_scheduler.py](../../vllm/v1/core/sched/async_scheduler.py))

reviews.body:
## Code Review

This pull request adds a comprehensive 'Scheduler' section to the architecture overview documentation, explaining the V1 scheduler's token-budget-based logic, scheduling policies, and preemption behavior. A review comment points out a discrepancy between the documented async scheduling preemption logic and the actual implementation, which could lead to duplicate output tokens if not addressed.

## Pull request overview Adds a new **Scheduler** section to the V1 architecture overview to give contributors an entry point into how V1 scheduling, preemption, and async scheduling work. **Changes:** - Document the token-budget-based scheduling model (and lack of strict prefill/decode phase separation). - Describe FCFS vs Priority scheduling and their eviction behavior under KV pressure. - Explain preemption mechanics and async scheduling concepts (output placeholders, token discard behavior). --- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. Learn how to get started.
